label: October 2026

biggest.lede: We move the clock back by one second as worsening Ebola outbreak and severe Australian storms increase immediate biological and climate risks.

title: Ebola Outbreak Pushes Clock closer to midnight
summary: The clock began October at 85 seconds to midnight and ended at 84 seconds, moving one second closer due to a worsening Ebola outbreak and severe storms in Australia. The single biggest factor was the accelerating Ebola crisis in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which heightened immediate biological risk.

sections.heading: What moved the clock
body: The Doomsday Clock was set closer to midnight by one second on 31 October, reflecting increased danger from a rapidly expanding Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, now exceeding 5,000 deaths and raising fears of continental spread.
Additionally, severe storms across Australia amplified climate‑related risks, contributing to the decision to move the clock closer to midnight.

sections.heading: Where the experts disagreed
body: No experts voted in opposite directions on any day in October; all assessments were either hold or worse.

sections.heading: What to watch next month
body: Monitor the trajectory of the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa and the response efforts, as well as the development of extreme weather events in the Southern Hemisphere, which together will shape the clock’s position in November.
